answer: To stop malicious swarms, an AI economy can require every new agent to permanently burn a scarce, non-transferable resource upon registration. When forging a digital ID demands an irrevocable burn as costly as rare jade or golden saffron, setting up fake crowds becomes ruinously unprofitable. Sybil attacks instantly fail because the price of spawning thousands of bots far outweighs any possible fraudulent profit. Consequently, system security achieves its zenith by turning identity creation into a severe financial barrier.
